items.title: Bloodborne gets Elden Ring's best feature in brand new free add-on
items.summary: One of Elden Ring's most notable unique features has now made its way over to Bloodborne, and it seems like the perfect excuse to replay 🌕
items.content:
Bloodborne now has a map system similar to Elden Ring's, complete with fast travel and custom markers.

Bloodborne players can now get one of Elden Ring 's most standout features in a brand new mod created for bbport.

It's certainly no secret that Bloodborne is one of the best games made by FromSoftware, and certainly one of the best games of all time.

For those who have played through the game dozens, or even hundreds, of times, there's a good opportunity to change up the experience thanks to mods which make changes to the unofficial PC port.

This new mod for Bloodborne brings over Elden Ring's map for use in-game.

Titled Hunter's Atlas, the mod brings over maps from every area in Bloodborne , complete with markers designating your position, the location of lamps and NPCs, as well as doors and ladders. You can also see pickups and other details on the map as well, if you want to.

It's obviously not an essential mod, considering the original Bloodborne worked well enough without a map when we all played it ten years ago. But for those wanting to load up a bunch of mods and get a different experience, this is one worth downloading.

Elden Ring 's map was a first for FromSoftware, which had previously opted to not include maps in its games like Dark Souls and Bloodborne . A map was technically included in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice , but we wouldn't say it was particularly useful in navigating it .

But with Elden Ring being the developer's first true open-world game, a map was seen as being pretty necessary to include to help players find their way around. This version included fast travel, icons for NPCs, and other landmarks to help you find your way around.

If you'd like to check out the Hunter's Atlas mod, you can download it from Bloodborne 's Nexus Mods page.

Read More: Steam drops free Bloodborne-inspired retro demo, scratch that FPS itch

Known as bbport, the unofficial PC port has been an option for many Bloodborne fans to check out the 2015 game on PC for the past few weeks .

It technically runs better than emulating the game using the PS4 emulator ShadPS4, and arguably is a little easier to set up. This version of the game allows you to play the original Bloodborne plus its DLC, at higher resolutions and framerates compared to the PS4 version. There are also mods available which allow you to enhance the original graphics .

With that said, you can only play it if you actually own the original game, so be sure you have the ability to dump your own Bloodborne disc onto your PC for use with bbport. If you'd rather not touch that, the original PS4 version is still an option, which is available to play on PS5 via backwards compatibility.

items.title: Alex Garland’s Elden Ring adaptation is on course to be Hollywood’s goriest ever fantasy movie
items.summary: The expansive project has hype and money behind it – but how do you avoid it falling into the disappointment trap so many films end up stumbling into?
items.content:
Too big to fail … Elden Ring Photograph: Bandai Namco View image in fullscreen Too big to fail … Elden Ring Photograph: Bandai Namco Week in geek Movies Alex Garland’s Elden Ring adaptation is on course to be Hollywood’s goriest ever fantasy movie Ben Child The expansive project has hype and money behind it – but how do you avoid it falling into the disappointment trap so many films end up stumbling into?

I f the history of failed Hollywood fantasy projects over the past 20 years has taught us anything, it is that transporting audiences to another world is only half the battle: you also have to give them a reason to spend several hours there. The Golden Compass diluted Philip Pullman’s theological bite, Warcraft thought that just explaining its world would make us care about it, and The Dark Tower compressed Stephen King’s sprawling mythology so ruthlessly that it scarcely left room for a story. All these films at one point had fans of the original source material quivering with anticipation at the prospect of seeing their beloved worlds on the big screen; all ended up disappointing.

Which brings us to the forthcoming Alex Garland adaptation of the hugely popular high fantasy video game, Elden Ring. If there was ever a cinematic test of the phrase “too big to fail”, it is surely this. Elden Ring has sold more than 30m copies and is widely regarded as one of the greatest video games ever made. George RR Martin himself wrote the foundational mythology of warring demigods that underpins its gorgeous fantasy hellscape. And Garland as writer-director seems almost impossibly perfect: as the creative behind Dredd, Ex Machina and Annihilation, he has both the taste for beautiful nightmares and the geek credentials to deliver something extraordinary.

View image in fullscreen Creative … Alex Garland Photograph: Monica Schipper/Getty Images for IMDb It appears the movie has already been shot and is in post-production, with a cast including Cailee Spaeny, Ben Whishaw, Nick Offerman, Sonoya Mizuno, Peter Serafinowicz and Jonathan Pryce. Amazon MGM has reportedly snapped up streaming rights across numerous international markets, while theatrical distribution rights are being touted at November’s American Film Market, where it will reportedly be the most expensive stand-alone project ever offered for sale. Deadline suggests the budget is close to $200m , which ought to pay for at least a couple of Elden Ring’s repulsive resident monstrosities’ more expensive mutations.

And that’s the thing about the game: it veers far closer to full-on horror than anything we’ve seen so far in mainstream Hollywood swords and sorcery. There are creatures with writhing worms for faces. There are enormous, bodiless hand spiders that scuttle about on eight or more fingers. There are mechanical iron maidens that hurtle towards you on wheels, swinging enormous blades, before their bellies spring open and a nest of snakes drags you into the machinery.

If the far more wholesome The Lord of the Rings was once considered unfilmable, what hope for a fantasy world where almost everyone is dead and the survivors are coping by eating their lovers’ corpses? Will there even be a hero in this thing for audiences to pin their hopes on?

In the game, you hack, slash and spellcast through a zillion dead things before taking on the various demigods in final boss battles, but that can’t and won’t be the extent of the film. Perhaps Garland will draw on the Martin-inspired backstory of how the Lands Between descended into death and destruction in the first place. Leaked images suggest a Leyndell (this world’s capital) populated by living people and hint at the execution of a hideous character known as the Dung Eater (a pre-game event), all of which suggests some sort of prequel might be in play.

It’s hard to see a happy ending here, but perhaps that’s the point. After all, Garland has a record of denying audiences conventional Hollywood-style reassurance. In Annihilation, he brought a married couple back together while leaving us wondering whether either remained human; in Ex Machina, he let the gorgeous AI escape and left her would-be rescuer locked up to die; in Civil War, he overthrew a tyrant but made the victory photograph look like evidence for a future war crimes tribunal. The uncertainty is whether he will get the same freedom with a film costing close to $200m. At the very least, prospective purchasers need to be aware that they are unlikely to be buying the 2026 equivalent of a return to the Shire. Unless, of course, they want a world where something has eaten the hobbits and is now wearing them.

items.title: 5 Best Video Games Like Lies Of P
items.summary: If you like the "Soulslike" gameplay of "Lies of P," we
items.content:
NEOWIZ Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Out of all the "Soulslike" spin-offs that have been released over the past decade or so, "Lies of P" certainly stands out from the crowd. Not only is the gameplay fluid, crisp, and more forgiving than other games in the genre, but the setting is something that the industry hasn't really seen before. Being able to take part in a twisted version of Pinocchio isn't something that gamers get to experience often, and the tough bosses only add to the unique plot.

However, given that "Lies of P" is a "Soulslike" game, there are other titles that offer a similar style of combat and gameplay or uncommon settings and stories. However, finding the right one to play if you like "Lies of P" is easier said than done, as some games feature a more comparable experience than others. Fortunately, we've put together a helpful list of the five best games similar to "Lies of P" right here.

FromSoftware It feels only right to kick off the list with arguably the most celebrated "Soulslike" game in the entire genre: "Elden Ring." While it might not be every player's favorite "Soulslike," there's no denying the gravity that "Elden Ring" possesses. It features one of the most intriguing open worlds of any video game, allowing you to explore a variety of different and dangerous regions that all house some of the toughest bosses in all of gaming .

To go up against these bosses, you'll have to kit out your character with the right weapons and gear for your chosen class. There are plenty of items to find through exploration or killing bosses, and the rune currency system in "Elden Ring" grants you plenty of opportunity to upgrade your character and try out different builds. It's difficult to describe the sheer scale of "Elden Ring," as its boss variety, open world, gear system, and weaving story are all beautifully implemented into a masterpiece of a game. Granted, it's more difficult than "Lies of P," but that makes the challenge all the more worthwhile.

EA On paper, it might seem like "Star Wars Jedi: Survivor" and "Lies of P" have nothing in common. One is set in the galactic "Star Wars" universe, while the other takes place in a twisted fantasy world of a classic novel. However, once you start playing "Star Wars Jedi: Survivor," you'll find that it has plenty to offer if you enjoyed the core gameplay loop in "Lies of P."

"Star Wars Jedi: Survivor" isn't considered a "Soulslike" title, but it does feature extremely challenging boss fights and general combat that requires the utmost precision. You'll have to rely on parrying, quick movements, and your abilities to escape in order to succeed in the major boss battles during the story.

The game lets the player control Cal Kestis, a member of the Rebel Alliance in "Star Wars" who travels the galaxy in his own spaceship with a crew of other rebels who are looking to take down the Galactic Empire. "Star Wars Jedi: Survivor" allows you to travel to open-world planets, meet some iconic characters, complete some surprisingly tough puzzles, and engage in truly gripping combat that will have you feel like you're playing a "Soulslike."

FromSoftware Thematically, "Bloodborne" is likely the closest game to "Lies of P" that you'll find on the market. Both games are set in grim and ruined cities that feature Gothic elements and 19th-century architecture. Even if you look past the similar visuals and setting, though, "Bloodborne" is arguably the best overall "Soulslike" from a gameplay perspective as well. While it might be tougher to beat than "Lies of P," the mechanics don't take long to pick up if you're an experienced player within this genre.

"Bloodborne" immediately hits the ground running, throwing you into an impossible combat situation and forcing you to figure out the game's mechanics for yourself. While the general controls are easy enough to understand, it will take hours to master the various elements of combat. Fortunately, you have access to a variety of mechanics and weapons, including a parry, firearms, and tons of melee options. As with any "Soulslike," the story takes a backseat to the combat in "Bloodborne," but there's still a narrative being told as you travel through the non-linear levels. However, one of the major flaws with "Bloodborne" is that it can only be played on PS4 or with backwards compatibility on PS5, and it's not available at all on PC or Xbox.

Sony If you're looking for an easier "Soulslike" that doesn't punish you at every turn, then you'll want to take a look at "Stellar Blade." There are several "Soulslike" mechanics in "Stellar Blade," such as using campsites to save and regroup, a parry system, and some shockingly challenging bosses, but the game isn't considered a full-fledged part of the genre due to some of its more lenient elements.

For example, there's no real penalty for dying, so you don't lose any currency or character progression if you happen to fall to a boss or other enemy. There are also a set of difficulty options that can make the game easier or harder based on your preferences. However, these features in no way diminish the overall experience in "Stellar Blade."

It's a fast-paced action-adventure game that sees you play as Eve, a futuristic soldier who's been sent to Earth to stop an alien force from invading. The combat is thrilling, often relying on combos to deal damage, and there's a semi-open world for you to explore and find plenty of collectibles and side areas to get lost in, away from the main story. While it's not a true "Soulslike," any fan of the genre can hop into "Stellar Blade" and enjoy its gameplay for what it is: fun.

KOEI TECMO GAMES "Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty" is one of the more unique "Soulslike" games in the entire genre, as it certainly features the difficulty level and other mechanics you'd expect to find, but it changes up the formula in a number of ways as well. For starters, the game features semi-linear levels that all start you with a certain ranking level, and you need to increase this level by exploring the area in order to make fighting enemies easier. You don't often see this type of exploration rewarded in "Soulslike" games, but "Lies of P" fans should be able to get behind this mechanic with no problem.

Of course, you'll also find plenty of common genre tropes in "Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty" as well. The bosses are extremely challenging, with some of the toughest ones coming early on in the story that force you to learn the game's mechanics, or you won't progress. The combat mechanics revolve around an in-depth parry system that you'll need to lean on constantly if you want to defeat any boss, but you also have abilities and melee weapons to deal damage at the right times. From a story perspective, "Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty" can be hard to follow at times, but the exploration and combat are strong enough that you'll want to keep playing until the end.

items.title: George R. R. Martin's New Dark Fantasy Is Already Bigger Than Peak Game of Thrones
items.summary: When Game of Thrones was at its peak, it was a fantasy juggernaut, but George R.R. Martin's newest adaptation will be even bigger.
items.content:
Image via HBO Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Fawzia Khan Published Oct 31, 2026, 6:00 PM EDT Fawzia Khan is a writer, editor, photographer, and creative producer. She holds a bachelor's degree in journalism and has worked extensively in the entertainment industry. She has previously worked at the photo desk at GQ Magazine. You can read her work in Elle Magazine, ScreenRant, The Wire, CLAD, Times of India, and DSSC. Her debut novel, part of a larger series, is currently in the works. Sign in to your CBR account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Through the 2010s, Game of Thrones was the standard for how big a fantasy world could look on screen. Now the man who built Westeros is attached to something that looks even larger on paper. George R.R. Martin wrote the mythology behind FromSoftware's Elden Ring , and A24 is turning that world into a live-action movie written and directed by Alex Garland.

This week, Deadline reported that the movie is heading to the American Film Market with a budget between $175 million and $200 million, which would make it A24's most expensive movie ever and, according to Deadline , the biggest-budget standalone project ever put up for sale at a film or TV market. The movie doesn't open until March 3, 2028, but in budget, universe, and big-screen branding, Elden Ring is already looking bigger than Game of Thrones was at its peak.

Elden Ring the movie is written by Alex Garland, which is based on the story and mythology that George R.R. Martin created for the game -- Martin also serves as producer alongside Peter Rice, Andrew Macdonald, Allon Reich, and Vince Gerardis. Hidetaka Miyazaki directed the 2022 game, with Yui Tanimura co-directing, and Bandai Namco published it.

When the movie was announced, the video game had shipped more than 30 million copies, and it swept the 2022 Game Awards, taking the game of the year, best game direction, and best role-playing game categories. This pedigree, especially the Martin lineage, matters because Elden Ring's world is designed to feel enormous. The game is a dark fantasy epic with sweeping environments and grim dungeons, and the movie's reported story follows Kit Connor's protagonist through monster and dragon battles.

Elden Ring is set in the Lands Between, a vast fantasy world once ruled by Queen Marika the Eternal under the power of the Elden Ring, a mysterious force that governs the laws of existence. When the Elden Ring is shattered, its fragments, known as Great Runes, are claimed by Marika's demigod children, who wage war against one another in a devastating conflict called the Shattering.

With the Golden Order thrown into chaos, the Lands Between descends into ruin, leaving its inhabitants corrupted by power and ambition. Players take on the role of a Tarnished, an exile who has been summoned back to the Lands Between by the guidance of grace. Tasked with collecting the Great Runes and restoring the Elden Ring, the Tarnished must journey across dangerous landscapes, battle formidable enemies, and confront the demigods who stand in their way.

The comparison with Game of Thrones is bound to happen. George R.R. Martin's novels fed a show that ran for 73 episodes over eight seasons. Elden Ring, though, has a different structure: a mythology born in a game designed to be explored over dozens or hundreds of hours, now set to be compressed into a single feature.

That is both its biggest challenge and its biggest source of potential. A world this dense can hide a lot of story, and Martin's involvement lends it a lineage that audiences already associate with epic fantasy. It also helps that the person adapting it is a fan -- Alex Garland struggled with the same Elden Ring boss fights that frustrated everyone else, so he understands what he's tackling and why longtime fans care.

Jon Snow battles a white walker in Game of Thrones. Image via HBO Looking solely at money invested, Elden Ring is already towering over George R.R. Martin's earlier masterpiece . The production budget is estimated at $175 million to $200 million, with The Wall Street Journal reporting it at the higher end of nearly $200 million.

For comparison, A24's previous record was Marty Supreme, at around $70 million. Even Alex Garland's own Civil War, which became only the second A24 film to pass $100 million at the box office, cost about $50 million.

Game of Thrones was an expensive show, but its numbers look vastly different set against this. The final season reportedly cost around $15 million per episode, so a six-episode season came to roughly $90 million. At those rates, Elden Ring's budget is equal to about 13 episodes of Thrones at its peak, more than double that entire final season. Except, this is for a single story that will be told in one sitting.

Garland's script runs a reported 180 pages, which could push the movie towards three hours. It's also worth remembering that an increased investment also means risk. A movie typically needs about 2.5 times its budget to break even, which would put Elden Ring ​​​​​​near $500 million worldwide.

Garland shot the movie over roughly 100 days, and World of Reel framed A24's strategy as chasing the majors' playbook: video game IP, IMAX, and a nine-figure price tag. That's a huge bet for a studio built on lean productions, and it explains why Amazon's early money matters. A24 is financing the production itself; Elden Ring is the talk of the market, with other international theatrical rights open to bidders at the Los Angeles event this week.

Elden Ring Raging Wolf Armor (2) Image Via Bandai Namco Where Game of Thrones lived on HBO, Elden Ring ​​​​​​is being positioned as a theatrical event. It opens in theaters and IMAX on March 3, 2028, and it was filmed for IMAX. This branding is deliberate, as Alex Garland is A24's resident big-movie director, with Ex Machina , Civil War , and Warfare behind him. The studio is clearly betting that his reputation for films with more depth than the usual blockbuster can anchor a franchise-scale release.

items.title: George R. R. Martin's Upcoming Epic Fantasy Movie Can Beat 'Game of Thrones' at Its Own Game
items.summary: George R.R. Martin's newest fantasy world is the natural evolution.
items.content:
FromSoftware Add MovieWeb on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Charles Papadopoulos Published Oct 31, 2026, 7:00 PM EDT Charles is the Lead Features Editor for MovieWeb, based in Brooklyn. After he began writing for ScreenRant in 2022 as a Freelance Writer for the Lists team, Charlie quickly rose through the ranks and became a full-time writer. This allowed him to pivot to MovieWeb. Sign in to your MovieWeb account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Game of Thrones is George R. R. Martin's magnum opus, and it always will be. But the veteran author has defined more than one fascinating speculative fiction world. Early in his career, George R. R. Martin was known as a sci-fi writer and built out his first fictional universe with interplanetary space opera novels like Dying of the Light . More recently, he contributed to the world-building that laid the foundation for FromSoftware's epic fantasy game, Elden Ring .

Copy this fact More things on this day I've covered George R. R. Martin's work professionally for half a decade, including extensive coverage of House of the Dragon and consistent analysis related to his novels. I'm also an avid gamer and fan of fantasy RPGs, and can proudly say I've overcome my intangible inability to be good at video games in order to beat Elden Ring .

One of my joys in the experience was exploring the mysterious, esoteric world-building the game has to offer and trying to pinpoint what might have been contributed by Martin versus what felt like a trademark of FromSoftware games.

Close Bandai Namco From Software From Software From Software window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-453824546"] = '" Close Bandai Namco From Software From Software From Software "'; Alex Garland and A24 are currently developing one of the most exciting projects in modern Hollywood, a live-action feature film adaptation of Elden Ring . Despite being in development for years, I still have no idea what this film is going to look like, what the story will be, and whether Alex Garland is the right choice to direct it. But those curiosities make me even more excited.

This is a deeply ambitious project made by a director I admire, based on a game I love, with world-building from the author whose work I've spent the most time analyzing and exploring as a professional. While Martin himself is not involved in the Elden Ring film, his name as the foundation of a fantasy universe is the perfect lure for non-gamers and the perfect benchmark to assure this project's scale and sophistication.

While Game of Thrones is a low-magic fantasy, Elden Ring is as epic and sprawling as it gets, with a world built on a mythological scale, with painterly imagery to rival The Lord of the Rings. Even still, this franchise has the emotional depth, complex human storytelling, and gritty atmosphere to appeal to the same audience.

Quiz 5 Questions Game of Thrones - Who Said It? Your Top Score -- Attempts -- Average 85% Users 1.4K Start Quiz 0 0 Report Error Found an error? Send it info@movieweb.com so it can be corrected.

Elden Ring 's fantasy world is dark, mysterious, and alluring in many of the same ways as Game of Thrones , and as one of the few titles I could imagine matching up with it in terms of complexity and art form. Fantasy is a contained enough genre, at least in terms of breaking through to the Hollywood mainstream, to where it's easy to chart the path and trends from The Lord of the Rings to Game of Thrones to modern titles like The Witcher that haven't panned out as well.

In the late 2010s, television became the clear best medium for the genre, but almost everything that has followed Game of Thrones has struggled to match the visual production quality necessary for audiences to fully become immersed in those worlds. With titles like Greta Gerwig's Narnia and Elden Ring , the fantasy genre could gear toward another cinematic trend, in which scale and spectacle overtake the political complexity of Game of Thrones as the main genre traits Hollywood studios seek.

I imagine Elden Ring playing out very similarly to the Dune films, where the adaptation doesn't capture all the political narrative and character complexity and instead focuses on mastering its visual storytelling, which could be quite appealing.

From Software HBO window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-2-1522494852"] = '" From Software HBO "'; It's almost like how fantasy authors responded to decades of The Lord of the Rings homages by pivoting to stories focused on multidimensional political narratives, which were then followed up by the more modern subversions that focus on defining new fantastical aesthetics, like Brandon Sanderson's books or Fonda Lee's Green Bone Saga, completely deviating from the norms of Tolkien's elves and humans.

Similarly, the next era of film and television fantasy could embrace darker and more abstract imagery, similar to some of the weirder '80s dark fantasy movies, expanding beyond medieval fantasy and what audiences know the genre to be. Elden Ring can not only rival Game of Thrones in narrative depth but also serve as a natural evolution, paving the way for the next big era.

If done well, this could be a movie that video game players flock to movie theaters to see for the big screen experience, and like Dune , offer something strange enough to evoke curiosity. Hollywood A-listers headlining helps, but it was ultimately the unique cinematic qualities of Dune that made the first two films such enormous hits.

Kit Connor and Cailee Spaeny aren't quite on the marketability level of Timothee Chalamet and Zendaya just yet, but it's worth noting that Chalamet didn't have his current level of box office success until the Dune franchise. Plus, Elden Ring 's unique world-building could lend itself to lesser-known actors.

items.title: 'Elden Ring' Creators' Next Fantasy Game Officially Delayed to 2027
items.summary: The Duskbloods, the next game from the creators of Elden Ring and Bloodborne, has been officially delayed to 2027. Read on for more.
items.content:
elden ring Image via FromSoftware Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Adam Blevins Published Oct 29, 2026, 1:28 PM EDT Adam Blevins began working in the entertainment industry in 2022 as a Staff Writer for Agents of Fandom, where he progressed to Senior Editor and interviewed talent from Marvel Studios , House of the Dragon , and Planet of the Apes . He joined Collider as a News Author in April 2024, was promoted to a Senior position in December 2024, and has written over 3,000 articles for the site, including exclusives relating to Avengers: Doomsday , The Penguin , Star Wars: Skeleton Crew , and more. He primarily writes about the latest box office numbers and the hottest movies and TV shows on streaming, while also covering superhero and sci-fi news. He has completed a set visit for The Chosen and even has several months of experience writing Gaming Features at ScreenRant . You can find him on X , LinkedIn , and Muckrack . Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There have been plenty of great games released in the last few years, but not many have had the same cultural impact as Elden Ring , which is still one of the most-played games on Steam and other platforms years later. The game was developed by FromSoftware, the same studio behind the Bloodborne and Dark Souls games, and it was co-written by George R.R. Martin , the legendary author whose writings inspired Game of Thrones . Elden Ring is even being turned into a movie courtesy of writer/director Alex Garland , and it’s confirmed to be A24’s most expensive movie ever , boasting a budget of nearly $200 million. The movie has already wrapped filming, but it isn’t coming to theaters until 2028, which leaves the post-production team with plenty of time to make the final polishes before it comes out.

Next up on the slate for FromSoftware is The DuskBloods , which is being developed in collaboration with Nintendo as a Switch 2 exclusive — this means that the game will not launch on XBOX, PlayStation , or PC. Since the game was announced in 2024, it was thought that The Duskbloods would be released before the end of 2026, but this is no longer the case. FromSoftware announced in a new press release this afternoon that The Duskbloods has officially been delayed to 2027 to give the development team more time to focus on combat, strategic depth, and player expression. There was growing concern that the game would be delayed when it was completely left out of the September 2026 Nintendo Direct show, which came after the game experienced server issues that prevented players from logging in.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

Alex Garland wrote the script and directed the Elden Ring movie by himself, but George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki are credited as writers on the project as well for their work crafting the story for the video game. A24 has loaded up a star-studded cast for the Elden Ring movie as well, with Jonathan Pryce , Cailee Spaeny , Tom Burke , Nick Offerman , Havana Rose Liu , Sonoya Mizuno , Kit Connor , Ben Whishaw , Jefferson Hall , and more all being tapped for key roles in the film. Casting details are being kept under wraps, but the movie is being described as faithful to the game and full of epic cinematic moments.

Stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of The Duskbloods and the Elden Ring movie coming to theaters in 2028.

items.title: Elden Ring fans are just built different as completion rates exceed most other games
items.summary: FromSoftware's Elden Ring is one of the most completed games of the generation despite its difficulty and scale.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Elden Ring fans are just built different as completion rates exceed most other games Published:

FromSoftware’s Elden Ring is the studio’s best-selling game by far with a 136% increase in sales over Dark Souls 3 . While sales are always a great indicator of financial success, the better proof of a game’s quality rests in how much time players spend with the game.

As it turns out, Elden Ring players are just built different compared to other fanbases. Not only is the game one of the best-selling games of the generation, a third of players have spent over 100 hours in the game. (This figures don’t include the just-released Nintendo Switch 2 version of the game.)

This comes from Alinea Analytics’ Rhys Elliot who revealed that the open-world FromSoftware game has sold 36.4 million copies across all platforms. Half of those sales were on Steam with 35% of sales on PlayStation, and 15% of players on Xbox.

While sales are interesting, what’s more interesting is that 26.9% of players, 9.8 million of the aforementioned 36.4 million, have spent over 100 hours within the world of Elden Ring across all platforms. Yes, this may not be surprising if you’re an Elden Ring hardcore player, but the vast majority of players do not spend this long in games they’ve bought.

For example, Baldur’s Gate 3, which has now sold 23.2 million copies across all platforms is another beloved game with a devout audience. However, only 50.1% of players have actually finished the game’s first act, according to Steam’s achievement tracking stats.

As per Alinea, 10.9% of Elden Ring’s players have grabbed every single achievement in the game on PlayStation. Additionally 10.5% of players on PC have every achievement on Steam, and 3.9% of Xbox players have grabbed every achievement as well. This means that 3.5 million players across the game’s 30.6 million players have 100%’d the game.

These figures outperform many linear, non-open world game, which is all the more surprising. With FromSoftware’s penchant for difficulty and the fact that it is a large-scale open world game, players are simply bursting to spend more time within its world.

These figures show just how popular Elden Ring truly is. A game’s long-standing popularity isn’t just reliant on sales, but how much people actually play it. To this day, FromSoftware’s open-world game has tens of thousands of concurrent players at all time, essentially the figures of a live-service game.

While stockholders have pushed from FromSoftware to spit out another game in the series, it’s not known if the studio is planning a numbered sequel. For now, FromSoft is working on The Duskbloods, a new PvPvE Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive game. Afterwards, maybe another open-world game is on the cards, we just don’t know.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Lewis later jumped to By Gamers For Gamers where he jumped to become EIC of VideoGamer and the host of the New VideoGamer Podcast prior to the website’s acquisition.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

items.title: Opinion: Elden Ring Is One Of My Favourite Games That I've Hardly Played
items.content:
I have started a new Elden Ring save file on four separate occasions now, and I have absolutely adored my time with each of them. And yet, despite putting 15-20 hours minimum into each new load, my current Switch 2 playthrough is the first time that I've managed to push through the 'tutorial area'.

I need to do some explaining here, because if you have never ventured into the Lands Between, then three save files and 60+ hours spent in a tutorial sounds insane. However, in the grand scheme of things, it's not that bad .

After pushing you through a very brief 'real' tutorial — one that introduces you to the basics of Elden Ring's combat and movement — your Tarnished avatar is funnelled into Limgrave and beckoned towards Stormveil Castle as your first major objective. However, rushing straight to the battlements will put you up against foes and challenges that you are severely underprepared for, so the game encourages you to instead take a stroll around the area and perhaps venture down to the locales south of it in the Weeping Peninsula.

Much like Breath of the Wild 's Great Plateau, this is the game's actual tutorial. But I cannot stress this enough, it makes Link's wakeup spot look tiny.

Limgrave and its surrounding areas are huge and so densely packed with things to do that one could happily play this zone as a game of its own. Heck, for my first three save files, that's exactly what I did.

I explored the nooks and crannies of all the region's catacombs, took on mini bosses and Minor Erdtrees, solved environmental puzzles to unlock new gear, and took on sidequests that involved storylines and platforming challenges of their own.

On my first save back in 2022, by the time that I finally pushed through the game's first 'roadblock' boss, Margit (yes, there is a way around him, but I didn't see that at the time), I was quite content with the 20-odd hours I had put into Elden Ring, and I went off to play something else. Save files two and three saw me go further still, through the game's first real dungeon and into the boss on the other side. On both these occasions, I polished off Godrick the Grafted (a proper FromSoft name, if I've ever heard one) with relative ease, but was deterred by what awaited me afterwards: the proper game .

Just like the first time that you paraglide off the Great Plateau and realise everything you've explored up to this point is just a tiny proportion of what the whole map has to offer, stepping into Lunaria of the Lakes is a similarly daunting task. The zone's entry point even has a vantage point vaguely reminiscent of leaving the Shrine of Resurrection, for crying out loud.

For save files two and three, the scope of what was to come was simply too much. I had had a wonderful time with everything I had played up until that point, and loved how it all culminated in a challenging dungeon and gruesome boss. Honestly, I couldn't bring myself to do it all over again.

Until the Tarnished Edition arrived on Switch 2, that is. I finally got around to starting save file number four a few weeks back, and believe me when I say, I have not been able to put it down.

I did my usual Limgrave exploration, ventured into the fiery Caelid region (and swiftly realised I was still far too weak for it), and steadily levelled up in various catacombs and hoard encounters. Unsurprisingly, I dispatched both Margit and Godrick in one or two attempts — I've played 'em both more than enough by now — and Stormveil was similarly breezy for someone who's spent so much time in it over the years. But then something unexpected happened: I kept playing.

Despite my previous cowardice, I stepped boldly into the uncharted waters of 'The Lakes' and I still haven't quit. As I am writing this, I have just polished off The Academy of Raya Lucaria (a dungeon that, as someone using a magic build, can get in the bin) and its Good Boi / Bad Gurl bosses, and I still want more.

Aside from the portability perk — I couldn't put this version down, even if I wanted to — the Switch 2 port itself is absolutely sublime. All those months of convention footage and delays had me worried that I'd never be able to play a game this reliant on reaction times with a choppy frame rate, but it all holds up remarkably well. Performance certainly hasn't been perfect, and I have encountered some substantial drops here and there, but I'm finding myself enjoying this version even more than my prior attempts on PS4 and PS5 (and I loved those attempts).

Having spoken to some friends that are absolutely head-over-heels for this game, I know that I am very much still in the early stages of what Elden Ring has to offer, and there's every chance that I'll butt up against another roadblock down the line and bring save file four to an end.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before playing.

MAIN UPDATE ADDITIONS

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

    [/*]

  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.

    [/*]

  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent: - Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle. - Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes. - Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau. Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital. Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

    [/*]

The "Tarnished Pack" release times are as follows: Steam: Friday, August 28 at 7:00 JST | 00:00 CEST | 15:00 PDT.

Weapons

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]
